labels.notes: Unmarked in the module docstring (written `bbsrem:previous_section_observed_only` at char 851, no ** mark in the first 4000 chars; the five bold occurrences are declaration docstrings beyond char 118000, as at HEAD). REPORT status partial and marked false, which is correct: the mark waits on OQ-120. No statement of an existing declaration changed. A signature-by-signature comparison of HEAD and the working copy (101 declarations at HEAD, none removed, none changed) shows four new declarations: exists_isLiftedDev_delta_sq_mul l.2368, GammaLinkCircle.IsLiftedDev.mem_dsFutureDirs l.2388, exists_gammaP_lift_fixed l.2400, exists_rp1Iso_not_isIso l.2586. Otherwise only proofs, the two imports and docstrings changed. (i), (ii) and (iii) are unchanged from T-bbs-hs-singularities. « Does not extend »: GX.exists_positive_negative (l.2445; statement as at HEAD) holds at every p in dS2, which is stronger than the paper's existential. Positive and negative are real, not vacuous. IsSpacelikePositive/Negative carry f = delta^k g with k >= 1 and g hyperbolic with a fixed point. not_isIso_of_positive_of_negative proves E^-1(i+(L)) nonempty and open and derives g = 1 from both inequalities, so no circle is both. In the proof, the positive circle really satisfies t < g t on the lifts of future time-like directions (timelike_spacelike_dir, mem_dsFutureDirs). « Same holonomy » holds in the reading taken: the lifted holonomies delta^2 g and delta^2 g^-1 are conjugate in G~ (kappa from GTilde.IsHyperbolic.exists_conj_inv, delta central), so by rp1Iso_iff_conj the underlying RP1-circles are isomorphic (exists_rp1Iso_not_isIso). The Gamma_p-holonomies A and A^-1 generate the same subgroup, but only by construction; SCOPE (h) discloses that the statements carry neither this nor the degree 2. One formal weakness and one framing issue in the question are listed as findings. Neither changes the truth of what is claimed.

findings.what: The RP1-isomorphism clause quantifies over arbitrary linear θ : TpHS C.pt ≃ₗ[ℝ] ℂ and θ' with no IsOrientedTangent. Its docstring says « whose underlying ℝP¹-circles are ℝP¹-isomorphic ». The underlying structure of RP1Circles is the one of an oriented θ (the structure that « does not depend on the oriented identification »), and an orientation-reversing θ yields the reversed ℝP¹-structure. So the statement as written also accepts a mixed-orientation witness and is formally weaker than its docstring and than SCOPE (h). It is true in the strong form: the proof's θ = θ' is the oriented one from exists_isOrientedTangent. The conjugacy clause of exists_positive_negative has the same shape, but that statement is HEAD's and the dispatch froze it.
findings.fix: Add `IsOrientedTangent C.pt θ ∧ IsOrientedTangent C'.pt θ'` to the ∃ θ θ' of exists_rp1Iso_not_isIso. This needs the construction exposed with its oriented θ (e.g. factor the body of exists_positive_negative into a lemma that also returns hθ). Alternatively disclose the missing orientation in SCOPE (h) and in the REPORT. Add the same conjunct to exists_positive_negative when its statement may be revised.

findings.where: lean-gx/campaign/T-bbs-hs-remark-existence/REPORT.json, labels[0].questions[0]; HSSingularities.lean SCOPE (h) and the checklist row « holonomy ⟨g⟩ »
findings.what: Question 1 offers « equal in G~ » as a reading distinct from « conjugate in G~ » and says that under equal lifted holonomy groups « the remark's own argument cannot produce such a pair ». That holds only if both circles are read through one common identification θ. A (Γ_p, ℓ(p))-circle's lifted holonomy is defined only up to G~-conjugacy over oriented identifications. θ' = B∘θ with B ∈ SL(2,ℝ) is again oriented (vol3_lin), keeps the developing map ℓ(p)-valued with D' = ν∘D, ν ∈ G~ a lift of [B], and turns f into ν f ν⁻¹; IsLiftedDev.relate gives the converse. (This is argued, not formalized.) So the closer's two examples have the SAME lifted holonomy δ²g: read ℝ/⟨δ²g⁻¹⟩ through θ' with [B] = toPSL κ⁻¹, since κ⁻¹ δ² g⁻¹ κ = δ² g. Per-circle « equal in G~ » therefore coincides with the reading taken. Relatedly, SCOPE (h) attributes the conjugate reading to OQ-120 (b), whose text is the lifted holonomy GROUP. The question is still an extension of OQ-120 (b), since it concerns the same phrase of l.927 applied to the second half, but as worded it could lead the author to rule on a distinction that exists only with a fixed θ.
findings.fix: At curation, reword the question and its OQ row as follows. With each circle's own oriented identification, « equal lifted holonomy in G~ » and « conjugate in G~ » coincide and both hold for the examples. Only with one identification common to both circles (a fixed L̃_p ≈ ℝP̃¹) can equal lifted holonomy not separate positive from negative. Optionally formalize: ∃ oriented θ θ' and one f with C.IsLiftedDev θ E D f ∧ C'.IsLiftedDev θ' E' D' f.

questions_check: Question 2 (degree): sound. Positive/negative is defined for k >= 1 (l.906), and the degree is even at p in dS2 (IsLiftedDev.even_of_nonneg, l.905), so 2 is the least possible degree and the construction has degree 2. Question 1: the readings are named and the question extends OQ-120 (b), but see finding 2 on the equal/conjugate distinction. SCOPE (g) is true: GX.not_every_cyclic_subgroup_is_holonomy is at GX/BBS/QuotientCircle.lean:705, and exists_rp1Circle_of_ne_one keeps f ≠ 1, by exists_rp1Circle_quotient. SCOPE (h) is true, except for the omission noted in finding 1.
